language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.
language.lessonRating: How do you feel about this exercise?

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Bonjour! My name is Elodie and I live in the north of France on my family's winery.
The winery has been part of our family for many generations. My grandma often tells me stories about the winery when she was a kid. Here is an picture of my grandmother when she was 10 years old.
In our winery we grow the grapes that we use to make wine. Grapes grow on plants called grapevines. All the grapevines together form the vineyard.
Back then, there weren’t as many sources of air pollution so they didn’t need to worry about the effect of air pollution on the grapes. My parents do worry about this.
The tricky thing about air pollution is that it's not always easy to see.
That's why I have some devices that can help us study air pollution such as binoculars, a pH meter and a cell phone.
Let's go outside and explore the vineyard and its surroundings.
Elodie! Don’t forget your notebook! It has some very useful notes you took on air pollution!

Did you know that air pollution is absorded by the clouds and becomes part of the rain? Air pollution makes the rain more acidic than normal rain. You can measure how acidic rain is with a pH Meter. It has rained all of last week. So I used my own pH meter to measure how acidic it was around the vineyard.
